gloss: to know (a person or place); to meet
notes: Irregular: conozco. conocer = know people and places; saber = know facts.

sentences.translation: I met her at a party.
It's not going to be easy.

notes: yo como = I eat (como is also 'like, as'). In Spain, comer also means 'to have lunch'.

sentences.translation: What do you want to eat?
Do you have a room available?

notes: tratar de + infinitive = to try to. se trata de = it's about.

sentences.translation: They treat me very well here.

gloss: to look for; to pick up
notes: No preposition: busco mis llaves = I'm looking for my keys. Past: busqué.

sentences.translation: I'll pick you up at eight.
I looked for you all afternoon.

notes: The negative of también: Yo tampoco = Me neither.

sentences.text: No es tan caro, pero tampoco es barato.
sentences.translation: It's not that expensive, but it's not cheap either.

notes: Stronger than querer. Te amo = I love you (romantic).
Also a noun: un joven = a young man; los jóvenes = young people.
Not the adverb solo (only). Agrees: ella está sola.
un par de = a couple of, a few.

sentences.text: Vuelvo en un par de días.
sentences.translation: I'll be back in a couple of days.
I need a pair of shoes.

sentences.text: Solo tengo un par de preguntas.
sentences.translation: I only have a couple of questions.
I just don't want to go.

notes: Also 'middle': en medio de = in the middle of. y media = half past.

sentences.translation: I'll be back in half an hour.
I'd like half a kilo of bread.
I did it in half a day.

notes: No tiene sentido = It doesn't make sense.

sentences.text: Tiene un gran sentido del humor.
sentences.translation: He has a great sense of humor.

notes: lejos de = far from.

sentences.translation: I live far from my parents.

notes: Feminine, but el arma (stressed a-).
¡Alto! = Stop! en voz alta = out loud.

sentences.translation: I don't have a single dollar.
How many dollars do you need?

notes: No te preocupes = Don't worry. Works like gustar: me preocupa = it worries me.
Te doy mi palabra = I give you my word.

gloss: to be left, to remain; (quedarse) to stay
notes: quedarse = to stay. quedar con alguien = to meet up with someone (Spain).

sentences.translation: There are only two days left.

sentences.text: Las oficinas están en el centro.

notes: Often figurative: mi madre me va a matar = my mom will kill me.

sentences.text: Mi madre me va a matar.
sentences.translation: My mom is going to kill me.

notes: ir a la cama = to go to bed.

sentences.text: Los niños ya están en la cama.
sentences.translation: The children are already in bed.

notes: además de = as well as.

sentences.translation: She speaks English and French too.

notes: Stem change o → ue: recuerdo. un recuerdo = a memory.
Always acerca de = about.

sentences.translation: What do you know about him?

sentences.text: Es un libro acerca de la guerra.
sentences.translation: It's a book about the war.

notes: Plural: luces (z → c).

sentences.text: No hay luz en la casa.
sentences.translation: There's no power in the house.

sentences.text: Las luces de la ciudad son bonitas.

sentences.translation: It's not the right thing to do.

notes: Stem change o → ue; past durmió. dormirse = to fall asleep.

sentences.translation: Last night I slept ten hours.

notes: No hay sitio = There's no room. Mostly Spain; also lugar.

sentences.translation: There are better places to have dinner.

notes: ¿Te ayudo? = Can I help you? él ayuda = he helps (ayuda is also the noun 'help').

sentences.translation: Shall I help you with that?
My parents helped me a lot.

notes: Like seguir: consigo, consiguió.

sentences.translation: I never manage to sleep well.

notes: More everyday than esposo.

sentences.text: Mi marido está en el trabajo.

sentences.translation: We want to live in peace.
Do you have plans for Saturday?

gloss: as much as (en cuanto = as soon as)
notes: No accent, not a question. cuanto antes = as soon as possible. cuanto más..., más... = the more..., the more...

sentences.translation: Come as soon as you can.
I'll call you as soon as I arrive.

sentences.text: Cuanto más lo pienso, menos lo entiendo.
sentences.translation: The more I think about it, the less I understand.

notes: lo peor = the worst thing.

sentences.text: Es el peor día de mi vida.
sentences.translation: It's the worst day of my life.

sentences.text: Mis abuelos viven en un pueblo.
sentences.translation: My grandparents live in a village.
There are a lot of villages around here.

notes: Also a form of vivir: vivo aquí = I live here.
¡Basta! = That's enough! / Stop it!

sentences.translation: What kind of music do you like?
I didn't sleep at all last night.

sentences.text: Te vi anoche en la fiesta.
sentences.translation: I saw you at the party last night.

notes: los Reyes = the king and queen; also the Three Kings (6 January).

sentences.text: El rey vive en un palacio.
sentences.translation: The king lives in a palace.

sentences.text: Mi perro se cree el rey de la casa.
sentences.translation: My dog thinks he's king of the house.
The king and queen arrived yesterday.

notes: pedir perdón = to apologize. Also a noun: el perdón = forgiveness.

sentences.translation: Oh, sorry! Did I hurt you?

gloss: to be missing; to be left (until)
notes: Works like gustar: me falta dinero = I'm short of money. hace falta = it's needed.

sentences.text: Faltan dos días para mi cumpleaños.
sentences.translation: My birthday is in two days.

notes: Stem change e → ie: pierdo. perder el tren = to miss the train.
Used to address a young woman, or a teacher.

sentences.translation: The young lady would like a coffee.
I'll be back in ten minutes.

sentences.text: Son las diez de la noche.

gloss: to take, to carry; to wear
notes: llevar + time = to have been (llevo un año aquí).

sentences.translation: Can I give you a ride home?
We've been waiting for two hours.
What do you have in the bag?

sentences.text: Mi padre está en el hospital.
sentences.translation: My father is in the hospital.
We have to go to the hospital.

sentences.text: En la ciudad hay tres hospitales.
sentences.translation: There are three hospitals in the city.

notes: ¿Tienes fuego? = Have you got a light?

sentences.translation: Put the water on the stove.

notes: Irregular: pongo, puse, puesto. ponerse = to put on (clothes); to become.

sentences.translation: Where did I put my glasses?

sentences.text: No hay nadie en la calle.
Conozco todas las calles del pueblo.
sentences.translation: I know every street in the town.

gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
notes: acabar de + infinitive = to have just done: acabo de llegar = I've just arrived.

sentences.text: Es la prueba de que tengo razón.

notes: Also 'royal': la familia real = the royal family.

sentences.translation: I have a lot of books at home.

notes: la orden = an order, a command; el orden = order, tidiness.

sentences.translation: I don't take orders from you.
I have orders to wait here.
I take my coffee without sugar.

sentences.text: Nos vemos en el café de siempre.
sentences.translation: See you at the usual café.
It was a very hard day.

notes: Stem change e → ie: empiezo. Past: empecé.

sentences.translation: I start a new job tomorrow.

notes: Common in Latin America; in Spain usually fuera.

sentences.text: El perro duerme en la cocina.
sentences.translation: The dog sleeps in the kitchen.

notes: Also a term of endearment: mi cielo = my darling.
¡Buen viaje! = Have a good trip!
detrás de = behind.

sentences.text: Ve tú delante, yo voy detrás.
sentences.translation: You go ahead, I'll follow behind.

sentences.text: Hay un jardín detrás de la casa.
sentences.translation: There's a garden behind the house.

notes: y cuarto = quarter past. Also the ordinal 'fourth'.

gloss: free (not busy, not taken; at liberty)
notes: Free = no cost is gratis.
No accent, not a question: lo cual = which (referring to a whole idea).

sentences.text: Llegó tarde, lo cual es normal.
sentences.translation: He arrived late, which is normal.

sentences.text: Es la razón por la cual vine.
sentences.translation: It's the reason why I came.

notes: Stem change o → ue. Me suena = It sounds familiar.

sentences.text: Anoche sonó el teléfono a las tres.
sentences.translation: Last night the phone rang at three.

notes: Stem change u → ue: yo juego (juego is also the noun 'game'). For music: tocar.

sentences.text: Los niños están jugando en la calle.
sentences.translation: The kids are playing in the street.

notes: en cambio = on the other hand. a cambio = in exchange.

sentences.text: Hay muchos cambios en el trabajo.
sentences.translation: There are a lot of changes at work.

sentences.text: La película empieza a las ocho.
Me gustan las películas de miedo.

notes: un millón de + noun: un millón de dólares.

sentences.text: La ciudad tiene dos millones de personas.
sentences.translation: The city has two million people.

sentences.text: Te lo he dicho un millón de veces.
sentences.translation: I've told you a million times.

sentences.text: ¿Dónde está el resto de la familia?
sentences.translation: Where's the rest of the family?

notes: Also a form of extrañar: te extraño = I miss you.
presidenta = female president.
Singular in Spanish: la ropa está sucia = the clothes are dirty.

sentences.text: Me voy a cambiar de ropa.
sentences.translation: I'm going to change my clothes.

sentences.text: Tu ropa está en la cama.
sentences.translation: Your clothes are on the bed.

notes: el agente / la agente.

sentences.text: Hay dos agentes en la puerta.
sentences.translation: There are two officers at the door.

notes: Usually singular: much information = mucha información.

sentences.text: Tus amigos son un poco raros.
sentences.translation: Your friends are a bit weird.

notes: en general = in general, generally. Also a noun: el general = the general.

sentences.text: Tengo una idea general del plan.
sentences.translation: I have a general idea of the plan.

notes: ¡Trato hecho! = It's a deal!

sentences.translation: Thank you for treating me so well.
I have a deal for you.
What do you use for your hair?

notes: tener derecho a = to have the right to. As an adjective: right (side); straight.
de todos modos = anyway.

sentences.text: No me hables de ese modo.
sentences.translation: Don't talk to me like that.
There's another way to do it.

notes: Usually lo demás (everything else) or los demás (the other people).

sentences.text: No me importa lo que piensen los demás.
sentences.translation: I don't care what others think.

notes: Plural noticias = news. ¿Qué noticias hay? = What's the news?

sentences.translation: The police are looking for the killer.

sentences.text: En la película, la asesina es la doctora.
sentences.translation: In the movie, the killer is the doctor.

sentences.text: ¿Dónde está el control de la tele?
